title: Presence
description: Where one session is and what it is doing, sent as the data of an automerge-repo ephemeral message on the document of the screen it is on (a manifest's own document, or the presence document from GET /presence). Never stored: the engine relays it to every peer of the same document on every replica, and a receiver forgets a session it has not heard from for ten seconds. A sender repeats its presence at least every three seconds while the screen is open, sends it again on any change (pointer movement at most twenty times a second), and sends leaving=true when the screen closes. A session is one browser tab or one terminal, not a person: one principal may have several. Nothing here is a record of a person; it is the state of a live session, and it ends with the session.

session.description: A random id for this tab or terminal, fixed for its lifetime.

actor.description: The principal, as GET /session reports it.

name.description: The display name, where there is one.

color.description: The colour this session is drawn in, chosen by the sender so every screen draws it alike.

route.description: The screen, as the interface's own route (for the web, the path).

focus.description: The field being edited, by JSON pointer into the manifest; null when none.

caret.description: The selection inside a text field, as Automerge cursors, so it stays on the same characters while others type; null when none.

pointer.description: The pointer, relative to the element it is over, so screens of different sizes draw it over the same thing; null when it is off the content.

at.description: When this was sent, in Unix milliseconds by the sender's clock; for ordering one session's messages, never compared across sessions.

leaving.description: True on the last message of a session, so others remove it at once.

path.description: A JSON pointer into the manifest: the control's data-cartograph-field.

anchor.description: An Automerge cursor where the selection starts.

head.description: An Automerge cursor where it ends; equal to anchor for a caret.

target.description: What the pointer is over: a control's data-cartograph-field, or a region's data-cartograph-region key.

x.description: Across the target, 0 at its left edge, 1 at its right.

y.description: Down the target, 0 at its top, 1 at its bottom.
